name: SWEDEN

flag.title: Swedish Flag
flag.note: Blue field with gold Nordic cross

lead: Sweden is a long northern country where forests cover half the land and the summer sun barely sets. It gave the world IKEA, Spotify, and dynamite — and recycles so well it imports rubbish for fuel. Moose roam the trees, Vikings once sailed every sea, and Swedish children eat meatballs with lingonberry jam for dinner.
geo: Sweden stretches 1,500 km from south to north — so long that southern farms grow strawberries while Arctic peaks stay snow-capped. Nearly 100,000 lakes dot the land and thick pine forests blanket most of the country.
In the far north, Lapland sits above the Arctic Circle. The sun never fully sets in June and never fully rises in January — and clear winter nights blaze with green and violet aurora.
animals: Sweden's älg — the moose — stands taller than a horse and wanders into suburbs every autumn. Sweden has around 300,000 of them, one of the world's densest moose populations.
Wolves returned in the 1980s after near-extinction, now sharing forests with bears, lynx, and wolverines. In Lapland, Sámi people still herd vast reindeer herds across the tundra each season.
culture: Sweden is obsessed with beautiful, useful design — IKEA, Spotify, Minecraft, and Skype all started here. Swedes celebrate every week with fika: a cosy coffee-and-cake break that is basically a national religion.

Midsommar is the biggest party: dancing around a flower-covered pole, eating pickled herring under a sun that won't set. In December, Saint Lucia Day fills the dark with girls in white robes and candle crowns.
history: Around 800 CE, Norse Vikings sailed east and west — trading, raiding, and founding settlements from Constantinople to Newfoundland. Sweden became a powerful Baltic empire in the 1600s, controlling much of northern Europe.

Sweden hasn't fought a war in over 200 years — one of the world's longest peace streaks. It built a welfare state where healthcare and school are free, and it now ranks among the happiest, most equal countries on Earth.
wows: Sweden has around 270,000 islands — most are tiny rocky outcrops in the Baltic Sea and along its coasts.
Sweden imports rubbish from other countries because it converts waste to energy so efficiently it runs short.
ABBA sold over 400 million records worldwide from a country of just 10 million people.
The Nobel Prize was created by Alfred Nobel, a Swede who also invented dynamite.
In 1967 the whole country switched from left- to right-side driving overnight at 5 a.m.
Stockholm's metro is called 'the world's longest art gallery' — 100 stations covered in art.
Swedish meatballs trace back to a Turkish recipe brought home by King Charles XII in the early 1700s.

myths.fact: Stockholm summers average 23°C and southern Sweden grows apples and strawberries. Only the far north stays truly icy year-round.
King Charles XII brought the recipe inspiration from Turkey around 1715 — it is influenced by Middle Eastern spiced köfte.
